dedupe_keys.name: aeolus long term aviation forecasting model for dutch airports

description: AEOLUS is the Dutch government's strategic long-term aviation forecasting model. For the civil airports with large commercial traffic (Schiphol, Rotterdam The Hague, Eindhoven, Groningen Eelde, Maastricht Aachen and, if opened, Lelystad) it estimates autonomous growth and the effect of policy on flight movements, passenger numbers and types, air freight, aircraft noise and CO2, plus nitrogen, particulate and other emissions during landing and take-off. It is a year-by-year model to 2060 that seeks a balance between demand, driven by population, economic growth and costs (fuel and sustainable fuel, EU ETS and CORSIA carbon prices, airport charges), and supply, with restricted runs that respect capacity caps and unrestricted runs. Since its update to base year 2023 it runs in Python with six modules: passengers (choice of airport, route, access mode, rail or car, or not travelling, over 106 world zones), freight (five segments, belly, freighter or trucking), aircraft movements with iteration when an airport's capacity is exceeded, noise (dwellings inside the Schiphol 58 dB(A) Lden contour), emissions and output for cost-benefit analysis. The ministry owns it and Rijkswaterstaat manages it; third parties can ask the ministry for permission to use it, and it is not published online. Caveats: coverage is national and long term, and results depend on elasticity assumptions. PBL used it for the WLO 2025 scenarios, the long-term outlook for Dutch aviation and the climate and energy outlook. Related: CBS airport statistics catalogued here.
